name: Project setup and reference calibration
build: Create repository, clean build pipeline, exact engine/package lock, provisional hardware matrix, naming/ID rules and a tiny motion test gym. Conduct the assigned licensed hands-on reference review.
assets: Capsule proxy, meter grid, neutral material, one floor, one moving platform, placeholder Ivo proportions; no bulk final environment art.
systems: Input actions, scene bootstrap, build metadata, basic telemetry and packaged executable.
playable: A packaged test gym launches and accepts keyboard/controller input; this is not yet a game slice.
tests: Fresh-machine checkout and build; aspect ratios; remapping; 30/60/120 fps capture; package compatibility and license review.
problems: Editor-only dependencies, mismatched package versions, wrong scale, no reliable target hardware, assumptions copied from reference footage.
gate: A second developer produces the same build from a clean checkout; director/engineer approve the feel-measurement plan and stack; unresolved commercial dependencies have an owner.

name: Movement and interaction prototype
build: Implement lane motor, run/stop/jump, ledges, crouch, ladder, light grip and constrained heavy push. Establish interaction sockets and moving-platform support.
assets: Proxy Ivo rig; floor/stair/ledge/ladder kit; trolley and grip handles; initial locomotion clips.
systems: Motor state machine, input buffering, collision queries, interaction selection and basic camera follow.
playable: A 3–5-minute obstacle course containing every ordinary traversal action.
tests: Jump range, frame-rate parity, edge catches, foot sliding, release/cancel behavior, controller dead zones and one-action assistance.
problems: Unwanted root-motion authority, slippery starts, moving-platform launches, jump input lost during landing, low tunnels trapping the capsule.
gate: All defined traversal tests pass on keyboard/controller at 30/60/120 fps; ordinary jumps have visible margin; no critical controller defects.

name: Central Hold mechanic prototype
build: Implement personal Hold, range warning, exposed-contact acquisition, atomic anchor transfer, support relief and a three-node station mock. Prototype the final control mode now, not in the last production quarter.
assets: Slider, rotator, hinge, anchor, support prop, exposed harness proxy and three-node console.
systems: Process state, owner graph, conduit path validation, station latches, snapshot serialization of Hold state.
playable: A 5–8-minute laboratory of useful Holds, one transfer, one relief and stationary node selection.
tests: 1,000 acquire/release/transfer cycles per process type; occupied-anchor rejection; range break; pause and reload; conflicting commands; station context change.
problems: Duplicated owners, force accumulation, bodies drifting while held, ambiguous latch release, station controls that feel unrelated to earlier play.
gate: No ownership violations or lost process states; fresh testers can explain personal versus anchor/station retention; finale interface has a viable prototype.

name: First complete puzzle prototype
build: Build P01 shutter and P10 staircase relief with recoverable failures, visible support geometry and an Orren proxy.
assets: Two puzzle mechanisms, service catch, ratchet, wall/bearer proxy, basic contact sounds and hand animation.
systems: Puzzle predicates, support tolerance, partial checkpoints, reason-coded invalid interactions and fast reset.
playable: Two complete puzzles with entry, failure, recovery and durable exit state.
tests: Five fresh formative sessions; confusion map; invalid support placement; softlock search; replay duration; save mid-relief.
problems: Players see a timing minigame instead of load transfer, hidden exact angles, support visually touching but logically rejected, rescues not reflected after reload.
gate: At least 4/5 players understand why the supported stair no longer needs a bearer; all reachable prototype states recover without debug commands.

name: Core gameplay loop prototype
build: Connect a short traversal, Hold puzzle, transfer, consequence and exit into one continuous graybox. Add the first version of scenario orchestration and sequence launcher.
assets: Reusable service/laundry graybox pieces, representative Ivo animation, temporary ambient layers and minimal UI.
systems: End-to-end movement/interaction/Hold, puzzle reset, camera volumes, local save and scene transition.
playable: A repeatable 10–12-minute game loop, not separate mechanic rooms.
tests: Pacing, first-time goal readability, absence of unexplained rules, completion without designer commentary and packaged restart speed.
problems: Long dead walks, similar puzzles back-to-back, camera movement hiding causes, atmospheric pauses that feel like stalled content.
gate: Director signs the core loop as worth extending; no unresolved rule contradiction; production does not proceed based on an attractive still image alone.

name: Horror and tension prototype
build: Stage an anchor inhale, wet-sheet silhouette, conscious restrained face and a quiet aftermath. Establish tension-state audio and nonlethal observation timing.
assets: One final-direction hand/porcelain study, sheet variants, face/eye proxy, breath recordings and lighting target.
systems: Tension presentation, occlusion state, gameplay/audio phase sharing, detail camera and accessibility equivalents.
playable: An 8–10-minute sequence that changes from useful control to unease without relying on a loud sting.
tests: Fresh participants report what disturbed them; muted-audio and low-volume passes; readability on a dim display; intensity options.
problems: Grotesque imagery without understandable cause, predictable startles, inaudible core cues, accidental comedy in body pose or facial animation.
gate: The human-cost inference is understood by most formative testers; atmosphere survives without surprise volume spikes; art/audio leads approve a reproducible target.

name: Enemy and creature prototype
build: Implement covered/exposed Custodian, perception and blocked behavior; build Porter path/capture/Hold loop; mock survivor refuge routing.
assets: Shared Custodian skeleton, coat/port proxy, Porter rig proxy, basket platform, opaque/translucent cover and capture clips.
systems: AI FSM, cover sensors, hearing events, harness Hold adapter, platform support, survivor safety gates.
playable: P13 trolley escape and P14 Porter crossing in graybox; a simple two-group evacuation test.
tests: Detection/recovery fairness; all AI states during Hold/reload; cover versus rendered appearance; capture telegraphs; NPC route deadlocks.
problems: Enemies know hidden positions, freeze clears awareness, Porter basket jitters, two-handed trolley interaction conflicts with Hold, survivor teleporting.
gate: Known taught solutions succeed repeatedly; no unexplained immunity; player can identify every capture cause; two-group evacuation runs 20 times without deadlock.

name: First playable environment
build: Build the laundry entrance and first transfer bay as a cohesive final-direction environment. Establish modular kit, materials, light, audio and streaming seam.
assets: Laundry kit subset, hero drying bridge, anchor, Ivo production rig, sheet/rack props, local VFX and audio.
systems: Lighting/render pipeline, collision/art alignment, asset import checks, one additive stream boundary and contact animation.
playable: A 7–10-minute environment segment with a real puzzle and consequence.
tests: Motion image quality, grayscale readability, shadow/AA artifacts, collision seams, texture budgets and render cost on baseline fixture.
problems: Beautiful but unreadable mechanisms, intrusive fog, foot sliding, arbitrary material highlights, unsupported render effects.
gate: Art lead approves the in-motion benchmark; engineer confirms a scalable rendering path; source kit and import conventions are ready for reuse.

name: First 15-minute playable build
build: Assemble the opening from apartment through first Hold, drum and early subfloor route. Prioritize coherent onboarding over final art everywhere.
assets: Domestic kit subset, Anja/transport proxies with recognizable cuff, brace, shutter/drum, opening gestures and alarm.
systems: Opening scenario, follow/wait behavior, pickup persistence, first-use prompts, all ordinary movement and initial checkpoints.
playable: The first roughly 15 minutes of the actual campaign, ending at a safe subfloor checkpoint rather than a forced timer.
tests: Five fresh players; time to first input, reason for pursuit, discoverability of Hold, visibility of the mother’s capture and control-loss duration.
problems: Players believe they failed to save Anja through poor skill, no motivation to continue, opening cinematic too long, brace pickup lost on save.
gate: At least 4/5 testers understand the immediate objective and basic rule; no onboarding blocker; recorded action time is inside the planned opening range.

name: First complete chapter
build: Finish C01-S01 through C01-S06 including the first pursuit and seamless laundry entry. Replace temporary rule explanations with environmental teaching.
assets: Complete opening gameplay props, Custodian covered variant, key Anja/Ivo animations, chase sound and transition dressing.
systems: Chapter manifest, all C01 checkpoint states, chase orchestration, persistence into C02 and chapter replay preset.
playable: The full nominal 20-minute Chapter 1 from new game to laundry entry.
tests: Three uninterrupted clean runs, all checkpoint reloads, failed pursuit recovery, chapter replay save isolation and fresh-player timing.
problems: Exit entry mismatch, chase requires an untaught action, death repeats a long narrative event, chapter art changes collision readability.
gate: Chapter 1 is feature-complete and navigable without debug tools; no critical progression or save bugs; remaining polish has bounded tasks.

name: First 30-minute playable build
build: Join Chapter 1 to the first laundry interactions and hanging-rack puzzle. Finish continuity of lighting, music, controls and save state across the chapter seam.
assets: Laundry rack pair, free anchors, transfer feedback, machine/breath callbacks and transition lighting.
systems: Cross-chapter persistence, shared asset references, anchor ownership across the seam and pacing telemetry.
playable: The first approximately 30–32 minutes through C02-S03. The label is a milestone, not a hard 30-minute stop in the middle of a puzzle.
tests: Fresh 30-minute sessions, seam profiling, motivation retention, repetition analysis and first full transfer comprehension.
problems: Repeated gate/bridge reasoning, a loading hitch at the chapter change, player thinks every anchor is safe or already understands the entire twist too early.
gate: Uninterrupted build with no seam blocker; first cost hint lands without overexplaining; controller and save behavior remain consistent across chapters.

name: Final-quality vertical slice
build: Finish all six laundry sequences to the actual shipping quality benchmark: movement, transfer, spatial puzzle, stealth, support relief, fingernail revelation and a streamed exit. Include release-quality menus needed to start/resume/settings.
assets: Final Ivo rig/materials, covered Custodian, complete laundry kit, all hero props, finished slice animations, mixed audio, lighting, VFX, captions and UI. No placeholders in the critical experience.
systems: All slice systems integrated; profiling, saves, accessibility, device changes, stream/load and automated fixture runs.
playable: A nominal 25-minute contiguous Chapter 2 at final intended quality. External tests can use a clearly separate 2-minute control familiarization area that is not counted as campaign content.
tests: At least 12 fresh sessions across skill/input profiles, baseline PC profiling, all checkpoints, replay loops, art/audio QA and one low-end quality pass.
problems: The game is polished in screenshots but weak in motion; unreliable physics; cost reveal not understood; interaction frustration; expensive art pipeline; scene requires manual cleanup to build.
gate: Director/art/audio/engineering/producer jointly approve. No critical defects; all essential actions/readability pass; documented frame-time and memory targets met or credibly rebaselined; per-room production effort measured. Otherwise iterate or reduce scope before bulk production.

name: Full end-to-end playable build
build: Graybox every remaining sequence, all 29 named challenges, all story beats, final network mode, root release and epilogue. Run parallel art production only on approved geometry.
assets: Proxy or production assets for the full cast, all unique mechanism types, surrogate water/deflector, root installation proxy, final animation blocking and temporary complete audio coverage.
systems: All campaign orchestration, narrative facts, every entry/checkpoint preset, evacuation routes, endgame ownership and completion saving.
playable: New game to credits without a developer console. Much art may remain below slice quality, but no chapter is a storyboard-only promise.
tests: Three full internal runs; fresh chapter tests; complete checkpoint sweep; duration ledger; narrative inference tests; brute-force softlock attempts; final input-mode transition.
problems: Finale feels like a different game, prerequisite flags missing, too much similar content, total length far outside target, proxy geometry disguises impossible animation needs.
gate: Every sequence has a playable solution and recovery; no debug skip needed; all essential narrative dependencies land; remaining changes are bounded before content detail multiplies.

name: Alpha: feature and content complete
build: Bring all rooms to complete playable content with first complete art, animation, audio, VFX and UI passes. Freeze new mechanics and narrative structure. Resolve geometry and camera changes now.
assets: All hero models, complete modular kits, full important animation coverage, every ambience/cue family, finished gameplay VFX and all text assets.
systems: Feature-complete controller/Hold/AI/save/streaming/cinematic stack; accessibility options; developer tools and logging for all chapters.
playable: The complete campaign with no missing gameplay content and no placeholder that prevents judgment of the intended experience.
tests: At least 8 new full-run testers; difficulty and duration distribution; complete no-audio/assist-mode routes; long-session memory; save migration from prior accepted schema.
problems: Late art breaks colliders; reveals too dark; cutscenes omit state on skip; inconsistent relief rules; players quit at a frustration spike rather than horror.
gate: Zero known critical progression/save defects; all essential assets integrated; feature freeze signed; pacing corrections and remaining polish are prioritized, estimated and funded.

name: Beta: complete, stable and representative
build: Complete quality passes across the campaign, localization integration, compatibility work and accessibility validation. Freeze content except corrections justified by test evidence.
assets: Final approved art/audio/animation/UI, localized captions/signage, legal credits and storefront capture candidates.
systems: Release-config builds, crash reporting policy, reliable suspend/reload, settings migration and validated quality tiers.
playable: A representative full game suitable for external usability and compatibility testing.
tests: Approximately 24 fresh full-run participants as a formative target; median duration 210–240 min, chapter bottlenecks, ending comprehension; hardware/input matrix; 20-session checkpoint stress.
problems: Long-tail puzzle stalls, inability to explain Anja’s fate, unreliable low-spec performance, captions spoil reveals, save corruption under interruption.
gate: No known critical or high-severity blockers; content/feature locks respected; timing target plausibly met without filler; all accessibility essentials and release dependencies accepted.

name: Optimization and final polish
build: Remove frame spikes, excess memory, shader hitching, animation pops, collision snags and audio repetition. Refine each chapter against the slice benchmark, not only the opening.
assets: LOD revisions, atlases, optimized shaders/FX, repaired contact clips, final mix adjustments and stable chunk manifests.
systems: Performance instrumentation, build stripping, asset validation, save compatibility and automated smoke suite.
playable: A near-final full campaign on all declared supported configurations.
tests: Packaged CPU/GPU p95/p99 captures, stress streaming, cold boot, disk contention, repeat deaths, credits/replay, installation and clean-user configuration.
problems: Performance fixes remove story detail, low settings change puzzle visibility, aggressive unloading breaks active Holds, last-week code churn introduces new save defects.
gate: Performance budgets satisfied on declared minimum; all critical regressions closed; no content changes without director/engineering approval and regression evidence.

name: Release candidate and final production build
build: Produce immutable release candidate, sign off rights/credits/storefront disclosures, test installation and updates, archive source/build artifacts and prepare support response.
assets: Final executable/content, store capsules/screenshots/trailer, credits, controls/accessibility descriptions, notices and support documentation.
systems: Release pipeline, integrity checks, crash diagnostics, rollback package, migration fixtures and reproducible build provenance.
playable: The exact intended shipping build, not an editor build or a different marketing executable.
tests: Clean-machine install, complete campaign, every checkpoint, offline play, controller disconnect, interrupted save, final release, credits and update/rollback rehearsal.
problems: Wrong bank/catalog version, missing licensed asset notice, marketing shows obsolete content, branch mismatch, a hotfix invalidates saves.
gate: No known critical/high release blockers; all discipline and producer sign-offs recorded; exact build hash archived. Any blocker returns the candidate to testing rather than being waived to meet the week number.

name: Post-launch stabilization
dependencies: M16; reserve window, not promised extra content
build: Monitor consented diagnostics/support reports, triage reproducible failures, ship narrowly scoped fixes and preserve save compatibility. Use reserve weeks for prelaunch issues first if needed.
assets: Patch notes, updated support FAQ, replacement assets only where required; no new campaign chapter in baseline.
systems: Issue triage, hotfix branch, regression suite, release rollback and save migration tests.
playable: The released campaign with critical corrections; the canonical story and duration remain unchanged.
tests: Reproduce reported faults on matching configurations; verify fixes against ending/saves and previous release data.
problems: Overreacting to isolated feedback, bundling risky new features into fixes, deleting user progress, promising dates before reproduction.
gate: Critical incident backlog cleared or mitigated; archive a supported baseline and decide separately whether ports or new content are funded.
